_expect.name: East Wall, North End (Diamond Dogs Area)

ca_east_wall_north_end_diamond_dogs_area.blurb: The north end of the East Wall in Joshua Tree's Hall of Horrors, near Sheep Pass at roughly 4,300 feet, is a large slab of shaded, mostly sound rock. Fourteen climbs are spread over it, nine of them trad, with three top-rope lines and a couple of bolted routes. Difficulty runs from 5.7 to the low 5.11s, with most lines between 5.8 and 5.10. Several of the best-known routes here are lightly protected, so it suits climbers who are comfortable above their gear. The surrounding formations of the Hall of Horrors tend to spread visitors out, so crowds are usually manageable.

_expect.name: Left Hand of Darkness - West Face

ca_left_hand_of_darkness_west_face.blurb: The west side of the Left Hand of Darkness formation in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree, at about 4,100 feet. It holds 14 climbs, mostly trad with a pair of top-rope lines, in granodiorite. The grade range is wide, from 5.5 up to 5.12, but the weight sits in the 5.11 range, with seven routes at 5.11 and above. It feels more tucked away than the road-side east face, though a few routes need some scrambling to reach, so it is a poor pick for young children. A short walk from the lot gets you to the base.

ca_green_wall_cliff.blurb: One of the main walls of Elephant's Graveyard, a high-elevation (around 8,500 feet) collection of single-pitch cliffs south of Carson Pass in the Mokelumne Wilderness. Fourteen routes here are mostly bolted, with a handful of trad lines. Grades cluster in 5.10 and 5.11, with one easier line and one 5.12. The namesake green wall looks north and stays shaded nearly all day, and the rest of the cliff drops into shade by early afternoon in summer, which makes it a good escape from midsummer heat.
ca_green_wall_cliff.parking_note: Leave the car in the last grove of trees alongside the dirt Forestdale Road.
ca_green_wall_cliff.approach: From the parked car, follow a clear use trail west for roughly 5 to 10 minutes until it meets the Pacific Crest Trail, then turn south.

ca_monkey_ball_2.blurb: A bouldering stop on the Highway 38 side of the San Bernardino Mountains, near Monkeyface Falls at about 4,600 feet. Fourteen problems sit on a huge white and gray granite block with a rust-colored stripe, and it is the most prominent group of boulders in the Monkeyface Boulders. Problems run from V1 to V8, with a good spread through the middle grades and a few hard ones at the top. Getting off the top means a downclimb followed by a jump onto your pad, and rattlesnakes have turned up along the approach trail in summer.

ca_p_the_fun_factory.blurb: A small sector of Riverside Quarry in the Inland Empire, set on the southwest side of the quarry beside Agony Arch. Of its 14 routes, 13 are bolted and one is trad, all on granite. Nearly everything falls in the 5.10 range, with one easier line and two at 5.11, so it is a friendly place for climbers building up to harder sport. Routes are fairly short and range from vertical to slightly overhanging with plenty of interesting holds. The wall faces south and is sheltered from wind, which makes it the quarry's warmest corner on cold days.

ca_midway_rock.blurb: A small outcrop on the trail toward Sugarloaf in the Highway 50 corridor, at about 4,460 feet. It is an overgrown boulder-like block split by a wide crack, and it carries 14 routes: ten bolted and four trad. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.11, mostly 5.10 and 5.11, with face climbing on one side and lieback and jam cracks on the other. It is one of the shorter Peripheral Rocks that line the Sugarloaf approach, so expect routes well under the height of the main spire, and it works as a stop on the way up or a modest destination of its own.

ca_may_lake_battle_tanks.blurb: A bouldering zone above May Lake in Yosemite's high country, at around 9,400 feet, known for steep low roofs. All 14 problems here are hard: the lowest is V6, most sit between V9 and V12, and the top end reaches V13. The climbing is powerful and sustained, with long roof moves and kneebars. Reaching it means hiking the May Lake trail to the lake, then following the trail along the shore until it begins climbing toward Mt. Hoffman. The cooler elevation makes it a summer destination.
